{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = "/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Step 1: Clean revenue column
# Remove commas and convert to float
# Handle the '999999.99' QA orders (if any)
# Also remove refunded orders
# Filter out refunded orders and QA orders

# First, clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
# But QA orders are flagged by revenue == '999999.99'
# So first, identify and filter out QA orders

# Convert revenue to numeric after removing commas
# Use errors='coerce' to handle invalid values

# Create a copy to avoid modifying original
df_clean = df.copy()

# Convert revenue: remove commas and cast to float
# Use errors='coerce' to turn bad values into NaN
# Then, filter out rows where revenue == 999999.99 (QA)
# Also filter out refunded orders

# First: convert revenue
df_clean['revenue_float'] = df_clean['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Identify QA orders: revenue == 999999.99
qa_mask = df_clean['revenue_float'] == 999999.99
qa_count = qa_mask.sum()

# Identify refunded orders
refunded_mask = df_clean['status'] == 'refunded'
refunded_count = refunded_mask.sum()

# Combine filters: keep only completed orders that are not QA
keep_mask = (~qa_mask) & (~refunded_mask)

# Filter the data
filtered_df = df_clean[keep_mask].copy()

# Now, check the final shape and sample
print("QA orders removed:", qa_count)
print("Refunded orders removed:", refunded_count)
print("Final sample size:", len(filtered_df))

# Now, check the distribution of channels and customer segments
print("\nChannel distribution in filtered data:")
print(filtered_df['channel'].value_counts())

print("\nCustomer segment distribution in filtered data:")
print(filtered_df['customer_segment'].value_counts())

# Check for imbalance: is the channel distribution balanced across customer segments?
# Cross-tabulate channel vs customer_segment
print("\nCross-tabulation of channel vs customer_segment:")
print(pd.crosstab(filtered_df['channel'], filtered_df['customer_segment']))"}
